findings: Covers every section in book order: lists (creation, properties, insertion, deletion, searching, uses), stacks (properties, push and pop, expression notations, infix to postfix, postfix evaluation, function calls, parentheses, undo), queues (properties, enqueue, dequeue, peek, BFS, task scheduling, print spooling, buffering), trees (properties, balanced, traversals, binary and AVL trees, uses), graphs (characteristics, properties, operations, types, NetworkX), choosing a structure, and combined structures (DFS, BFS, list reversal). None repeats the chapter exercise. Every program was run in Python 3 and its real output used. Book corrections followed: insert(), append(), pop(), index() (not insertf/append!/popO/indexO), q.get(), the corrected FamilyTree program, prefix +AB, Notepad, Figure 4.8 with 2 on the left, Figure 4.10 with 15 on the left; the doubtful 'John McCarthy 1960' box is not used.
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
